selected_problem: Fresh canonical main bound a hash-consistent apply receipt to the persisted changeset, but rollback still trusted each change.after.sha256 as the live postimage conflict baseline without revalidating that after.sha256/after.size/after.contentBase64 remained internally consistent. A coherently rehashed receipt plus a forged after.sha256 could therefore make externally modified live content appear to be the expected applied postimage and permit rollback to overwrite it.
decision_basis: The changeset already defines after.sha256/after.size/after.contentBase64 as one transactional postimage, and stagedAfterBytes already enforces this invariant at apply; reusing it during rollback closes the same existing invariant rather than choosing a new architecture.

The fresh-main defect is directly falsifiable by externally changing the live file, rewriting only after.sha256 plus the matching apply-receipt sha row/hash, and observing rollback accept the forged baseline even though after.contentBase64 still proves the original applied bytes.

Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained temporarily unavailable with HTTP 502, so this cycle uses DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY（DWAC 源码契约重放） plus exact local focused validation and does not claim hosted execution success.

pre_fix_reality.focused_reproduction: Fresh-main focused test failed with Missing expected exception: rollback accepted the coherently rebound after.sha256/apply receipt and restored the preimage over externally changed live content.
pre_fix_reality.impact: rollback conflict detection could be weakened by a persisted postimage metadata inconsistency that the changeset's own staged bytes were sufficient to expose

change: Rollback now executes stagedAfterBytes(change) during preflight before using change.after.sha256 as its expected live postimage. Writes therefore require persisted postimage bytes, size and sha256 to remain self-consistent; deletes retain the existing null/zero postimage invariant.

truth_boundary: This revalidates the persisted postimage's internal bytes/size/hash consistency before rollback trusts its hash as the live-state baseline. It is not an authenticated signature or external trust root and does not claim protection against a coherent rewrite of the complete changeset, its bytes, and its matching receipts.
